head: 0b52f186fb4af8fa7d4f6a71967f922eb6b69cdc

source.ref: https://github.com/ollama/ollama/pull/10135; AACR-Bench dataset.json rows 1233, 1234, 1235, forbid seeds 2058, 2059, 2060; licence MIT read from LICENSE at head; hand-checked 2026-10-23 by vetter A; the merged squash d931ee8f22 renders the last rows instead of the first

rationale: The change uploads model files in parallel, one progress spinner per file, and caps the progress block at the terminal height. row-1235 is required: at head render draws the first termHeight-1 states, so with more files than rows the newest progress and the final success status never show; the pull request's merged version draws the last rows instead (author-fix, first stated by a model). row-1234 is dropped: go.mod declares go 1.24, so the range loop's f and digest are per iteration and the goroutines do not share them; being false and a classic false positive, it becomes a forbid range on the loop header. row-1233 is dropped: replacing the mutex-guarded map with a slice is a refactoring with no measurable cost (one lock per uploaded file), and upstream kept a mutex-guarded map (types/syncmap). Forbid seeds: 2058 (mutex unnecessary) is false, since concurrent writes to a Go map need it, and kept; 2059 (worker limit defeats parallelism) is kept, since the limit is never below 1 and sequential uploads on small machines are what the code did before, a bound upstream kept; 2060 (redundant files map in CreateRequest) is dropped: false, since the handler needs the full paths to upload, but a refactoring idea no reviewer is asked to raise.

expect.concern: render draws only the first termHeight-1 progress states, so once a create has more states than the terminal has rows (one copy spinner per model file, then the server's statuses), the newest lines, including the final success status, are never shown.

forbid.reason: The module declares go 1.24, so each iteration of the range loop has its own f and digest and the upload goroutines never see another iteration's values.
The mutex is needed: the upload goroutines write the shared Files and Adapters maps concurrently, which a Go map does not allow unguarded.
The worker limit is never below 1, so on one or two cores the uploads run one at a time as they did before the change; the bound is deliberate and was kept upstream, not a regression.
